title: Interlocks in Ladder: a reversing motor
summary: Edit two Ladder rungs so that a reversing motor never closes its Forward and Reverse contactors together, and a lost lubrication permissive drops either direction.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show a safety function, mechanically interlocked contactors or wiring.
objectives: Tell an interlock, a contact that keeps one output off while another is on, from a permissive, a contact that must be closed for an output to run at all.
Lock two coils out of each other, so that one can never run while the other is on, together with Stop and the permissive.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/Reversing.ld.json two rungs are drawn, one per direction. Each holds its coil on with a seal-in under its pushbutton, and has StopPB and the permissive LubeOk in series. Add the interlock: Forward must never turn ON while Reverse is ON, and Reverse never while Forward is ON.
stages.checkpoint: Forward and Reverse are never ON together, a running direction ignores the other pushbutton, and losing LubeOk drops either one.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Forward starts at {{t:10}} ms. Predict Forward and Reverse at {{t:30}} ms, when RevPB is pressed while Forward runs, at {{t:90}} ms, when FwdPB is pressed while Reverse runs, and at {{t:110}} ms, when LubeOk drops.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:Reversing.Forward=true,Reversing.Reverse=false@30|Forward ON, Reverse OFF}} at {{t:30}} ms; {{v:Reversing.Forward=false,Reversing.Reverse=true@90|Forward OFF, Reverse ON}} at {{t:90}} ms; {{v:Reversing.Forward=false,Reversing.Reverse=false@110|both OFF}} at {{t:110}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}: The starter has no interlock, so pressing RevPB at {{t:30}} ms while Forward runs closes Reverse as well and both contactors are ON. Each direction must stay OFF while the other one runs, and the stop, the permissive and the seal-in of each rung must keep working as they do. Make the change in the Ladder editor.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named Reversing and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:30}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:70}} ms: RevPB is ignored at {{t:30}} ms while Forward runs, Stop drops Forward at {{t:50}} ms, and only then does RevPB start Reverse at {{t:70}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: Reverse falls once at {{t:110}} ms when LubeOk drops, and does not restart at {{t:120}} ms when LubeOk returns; a new FwdPB press starts Forward at {{t:130}} ms.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Once it passes, follow the power through the Reverse rung while Forward runs and RevPB is pressed: what does the contact you added read, and what would change if it read something else? And why must LubeOk sit in series before the coil and not only in the start path? Move LubeOk into the start branch and see which assertion fails.
stages.checkpoint: You can say what the contact you added reads in each rung, and what would differ if it read something else. A permissive in the start path only lets a running motor ignore it. The scenario shows the logic only; real reversing starters also use mechanically interlocked contactors, and this is not a safety function.

hints.text: Look at the two direction rungs side by side, and at what each of them does while Forward runs and RevPB is pressed.

In the Forward rung add a normally closed contact on Reverse between LubeOk and the coil; in the Reverse rung add a normally closed contact on Forward in the same place. Leave StopPB, LubeOk and the seal-in contacts where they are.

faultCases: The starter has no interlock, so pressing RevPB at {{t:30}} ms while Forward runs closes Reverse as well and both contactors are ON.
